policy.authority: Same-machine SP11 Windows is authoritative for hardware behavior. Upstream sources are vocabulary/implementation references only.
policy.runtime_rule: Any runtime_critical UNVERIFIED fact blocks bounded_first_pix runtime.
policy.production_rule: Any production_critical UNVERIFIED fact blocks production parity.
policy.linux_implementation_rule: LINUX_IMPLEMENTATION facts must set parity_claim=false and state an equivalence_basis.
policy.evidence_hash_domain: SHA-256 of canonical Git-index blob bytes; checkout CRLF/autocrlf is intentionally ignored

rejected_unproven_candidates.reason: The earlier upstream-only assertion that SID 0x18a0 was the RT-CDM requester was correctly rejected as proof. It is now superseded by a separate same-machine Windows derivation from qciommuext S1AG grouping + live IORT + installed qcsmmu + the accepted RT-CDM1 activity oracle; upstream naming remains corroboration only.

facts.claim: Front RGB physical route is IMX681 -> CSIPHY2 -> CSID1 -> IFE1/VFE1; VFE0 is inactive.
facts.linux_use: Select CSIPHY2, CSID1 IPP and VFE1 only for the front parity path.

facts.claim: Accepted front sensor mode is RAW10 VC0 3840x2640, one-trio C-PHY; stream-on/off is IMX681 0x0100=1/0.
facts.linux_use: Program the independently written IMX681 driver to the observed mode and lifecycle.

facts.claim: CSID1 IPP receives VC0/DT0x2b RAW10 and uses CFG0=0x802b2000, CFG1=0x00007241 with 3840x2160 crop/measure.
facts.linux_use: Use the observed IPP tuple and values; do not route parity through RDI.

facts.claim: Windows start total order is ISP_START_DONE -> MIPI_START -> MIPI_START_DONE -> sensor stream-on.
facts.linux_use: Linux parity orchestration must not start sensor transmission before the observed ISP/MIPI prefix.

facts.claim: ISP_STOP_DONE precedes both MIPI stop and sensor stream-off; Windows did not establish an order between the final two.
facts.linux_use: Use an observed-valid tail serialization only; do not claim the sensor-vs-MIPI tail order is mandatory.

facts.claim: Linux maps a 0xf000 VFE1 aperture. Windows command evidence requires at least through +0xbe70; 0xf000 is a Linux coverage choice, not a Windows literal.
facts.linux_use: Keep the Denali-only mapping large enough for the Windows-observed command span.
facts.equivalence_basis: Covers every observed Windows VFE1 offset while preserving Denali instance isolation.

facts.claim: Front VIDEO/FULL output is 2560x1440 QC10C/TP10-UBWC with stride 3584, size 0x76b000 and observed Y/C metadata/data offsets.
facts.linux_use: Represent the userspace surface exactly; captured Windows IOVAs are not constants.

facts.claim: VFE1 BUS static client configuration and FULL WM0/WM1 geometry are pinned from same-machine Windows.
facts.linux_use: Use public register names only as vocabulary; values/order come from the Windows capture.

facts.claim: qccamisp8380 live writer programs the nine-client address bundle in the proven order; FULL image/meta sites and cadence are closed.
facts.linux_use: Patch Linux DMA IOVAs into the same observed client/address fields; never reuse Windows allocation addresses or ring geometry.

facts.claim: VIDEO owns FULL Y/C + DS4 + DS16; stats use independent group FIFOs with no required cross-group completion order.
facts.linux_use: Linux may model independent software ownership as long as per-group FIFO semantics and VIDEO return ownership are preserved.

facts.claim: Epoch0 is BUS status1 bit21 and VIDEO is TOP status1 bit0, with exact Windows clear registers/semantics.
facts.linux_use: Bounded PIX diagnostics may poll only these proven raw bits; no other event bit is inferred.

facts.claim: Front uses hardware RT_CDM1 v2.1 at physical 0x0ac26000, FIFO0, with dedicated firmware GSI 319.
facts.linux_use: Bind the Denali RT-CDM resource to the observed block and interrupt identity.

facts.claim: Linux represents RT_CDM1 as a 4 KiB resource. The page span is a bounded Linux mapping choice, not a Windows-proven allocation size.
facts.linux_use: Map only the observed RT_CDM1 page and do not cross into neighboring RT_CDM0/unknown space.
facts.equivalence_basis: Windows locates RT_CDM0/1 on adjacent pages; public v2.1 register vocabulary is bounded within the selected page.

facts.claim: RT_CDM1 raw firmware GSI is 319; Linux SPI cell 287 is mechanically namespace-crosschecked. Windows descriptor class matches the known edge/latched camera resources.
facts.linux_use: Use GIC_SPI 287 with edge-rising encoding and keep the IRQ disabled until explicitly armed.

facts.claim: IRQF_TRIGGER_RISING | IRQF_NO_AUTOEN is the Linux request policy.
facts.linux_use: Preserve Windows-observed edge semantics while making Linux arm/disarm explicit.
facts.equivalence_basis: Trigger encoding follows the Windows raw descriptor class; NO_AUTOEN is Linux safety ownership.

facts.claim: RT-CDM open/reset/core-start, FIFO0 commit and stream-stop MMIO order/literals are recovered from the exact Windows driver.
facts.linux_use: Do not synthesize FE/FIFO defaults, optional CGC writes, CORE_EN=0 stop, or unobserved MMIO.

facts.claim: FE_CFG=0x07ff000f and FIFO0_CFG=0x01000000 are already present before the front CDM-object path; ultimate firmware/reset ownership is unresolved.
facts.linux_use: Linux may read/validate these exact values and fail closed, but must not synthesize/write them.

facts.claim: Whether firmware or hardware reset/default ultimately owns FE_CFG/FIFO0_CFG is not established.
facts.linux_use: No production implementation may claim or program the unknown owner; current bounded code only validates.
facts.blocking_reason: Production provenance remains incomplete, but bounded runtime does not write these registers.

facts.claim: Windows RT-CDM handler does not read IRQ_CONTEXT_STATUS; it masks FIFO status with 0x00070007 and acknowledges masked status then CLEAR_CMD.
facts.linux_use: Linux must not gate FIFO completion on an invented context bit.

facts.claim: Windows reads/acknowledges FIFO0..3 status banks; masked FIFO0 alone gates dispatch/completion.
facts.linux_use: Acknowledge all four known banks, but derive completion only from FIFO0.

facts.claim: RT-CDM BL descriptors carry the observed 32-bit command-buffer address fields; Linux rejects DMA addresses above 32 bits.
facts.linux_use: Fail closed on an address that cannot be represented in the Windows descriptor format.

facts.claim: Exact same-machine qcsmmu configuration assigns VFE client CB16/VM4 S1_IFE_HLOS to SID 0x0800 mask 0x0060 plus SID 0x18a0 mask 0; CB17/VM4 S1_ICP_IPE_BPS_CDM maps 0x1800/0x60, 0x1900/0 and 0x1980/0x20.
facts.linux_use: Treat 0x18a0 as a real Windows VFE/IFE HLOS SMMU route. Do not yet call it the RT-CDM1 fetch SID without the narrower requester proof.

facts.claim: Same-machine Windows mechanically identifies the accepted front RT-CDM1 IFE command-fetch requester as SID 0x18a0 in CB16 / S1_IFE_HLOS.
facts.linux_use: Use SID 0x18a0 as the Windows-proven RT-CDM1 command requester. This closes requester identity only; Linux DMA-domain wiring remains an independently classified implementation fact.

facts.claim: The historical integrated X1E CAMSS IOMMU list was stale and omitted 0x18a0. Static 0041 replaces it with the public five-entry S1 HLOS set 0x800/0x60, 0x820/0x60, 0x840/0x60, 0x860/0x60, 0x18a0/0; candidate is built but not deployed.
facts.linux_use: The 0041 candidate makes dma_alloc_coherent(camss->dev, ...) use the CAMSS IOMMU DMA domain containing all five declared fwspec streams. This is Linux implementation evidence only; exact RT-CDM1 requester->SID still gates runtime.
facts.equivalence_basis: Public X1E CAMSS v13 uses this exact five-entry implementation set; same-machine Windows qcsmmu independently proves 0x18a0/mask0 belongs to VFE/IFE HLOS CB16. The exact RT-CDM1 requester->SID relation remains separately unverified.

facts.claim: Linux 0041 declares the five-entry X1E CAMSS IOMMU fwspec including SID 0x18a0, and Linux DMA-core/SMMU inspection proves dma_alloc_coherent(camss->dev, ...) allocates an IOVA in that CAMSS device translation domain.
facts.linux_use: The Linux CAMSS coherent command-buffer IOVA is visible through the same CAMSS translation domain that contains the Windows-proven RT-CDM1 requester SID 0x18a0. This is an independently verified Linux implementation equivalence, not a Windows literal.
facts.equivalence_basis: Same-machine Windows proves RT-CDM1 front IFE command fetch uses SID 0x18a0/CB16 S1_IFE_HLOS. Linux 0041 includes 0x18a0 in the CAMSS device fwspec, and Linux DMA/SMMU code inspection proves CAMSS coherent allocations use the same device translation domain containing all fwspec streams.

facts.claim: Four startup command streams contain the pinned command/write/DMI topology; Linux materializes normalized templates and repatches local DMA addresses.
facts.linux_use: Captured allocator geometry and Windows IOVAs remain forbidden as Linux constants.

facts.claim: Only two logical period_cfg inputs remain dynamic across startup: packet0 value0; packets1/2/3 share value1. Their upstream formula remains opaque.
facts.linux_use: Treat both as explicit provider/test inputs; do not invent a Linux formula.

facts.claim: Exact startup/priming interleave is startup0 -> prime0 -> startup1 -> BUS -> prime1 -> startup2 -> startup3 -> CSID1 -> ISP done -> MIPI/sensor -> prime2 -> prime3/steady cadence.
facts.linux_use: Use the closed ordering; do not reorder from generic CAMSS assumptions.

facts.claim: For the first VIDEO: sensor-on -> Epoch0#0 -> complete BUS retarget -> replay2/request2 -> VIDEO; replay3 waits for Epoch0#1.
facts.linux_use: A bounded one-frame runner must stop before replay3/steady work if it returns after first VIDEO.

facts.claim: Selector-2 replay0..3 are complete 4/5/5/5-BL batches, not main-list-only submits.
facts.linux_use: Materialize and submit complete Linux-owned companion BLs with byte_count-1 lengths.

facts.claim: Steady Epoch0 uses five-BL batches and five observed main-list variants with captured DMI topology and GEN_IRQ request tagging.
facts.linux_use: Materialize local DMA with explicit module inputs; do not freeze captured payloads as production constants.

facts.claim: Exact Surface QcDeviceMFT/CamX Titan680 builders own the named changing register/DMI groups.
facts.linux_use: Linux consumer boundaries may name the observed module inputs without claiming proprietary algorithm equivalence.

facts.claim: Linux does not reproduce the Windows live IQ feedback algorithms that generate changing module values/payloads.
facts.linux_use: For bounded oracle experiments use explicit same-machine captured inputs only; production parity requires an independently implemented provider strategy.
facts.blocking_reason: Production image-quality/provider work remains open; not the immediate first-frame transport gate.

facts.claim: Compact Linux command/DMI arenas, frame slots and software ownership queues are Linux implementation choices rather than Windows allocator geometry.
facts.linux_use: They are acceptable only if every hardware-visible descriptor/value matches Windows and requester DMA visibility is proven.
facts.equivalence_basis: Windows allocator addresses/strides are intentionally not copied; hardware-visible command bytes and addresses are repatched locally.

facts.claim: Atomic one-shot gating, hash preflight and Golden rollback are Linux lab safety mechanisms, not Windows behavior.
facts.linux_use: Keep these safety gates outside the parity claim.

facts.claim: The successful Linux RDI frame proves sensor/CSI transport only and is explicitly not Windows PIX/QC10C parity.
facts.linux_use: Never use the RDI success as evidence for RT-CDM/VFE1 PIX DMA or processing parity.
